channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Bezos and Gates-backed mining firm locked in data dispute over Congo mineral archives in Belgium
item.description: The mineral-rich subsoil of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the centre of a growing international dispute, as US mining firm KoBold Metals presses for access to century-old geological records currently held in Belgium.

item.title: Kenya says over 1,000 of its citizens were recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine
item.description: More than 1,000 Kenyans have been recruited to fight on Russia’s side in the war in Ukraine, about five times higher than earlier official estimates.

item.title: Egypt to invest $4 billion in oil refinery upgrades to cut fuel imports and boost capacity
item.description: Egypt is investing $4 billion to modernize and expand its oil-refining sector in a bid to strengthen energy security, boost local value creation, and curb costly fuel imports. Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi said the plan involves six refinery-upgrade projects designed to raise national refining capacity and enhance efficiency.

item.title: Landlocked Mali to access the sea through Senegal River in landmark trade project
item.description: Mali is preparing to make history. For the first time, the landlocked West African nation will gain direct access to the sea through a new navigation route along the Senegal River, a project set to reshape trade across the region.

item.title: UK bank announces sale of Botswana subsidiary as top African banks bid for takeover
item.description: Standard Chartered has launched a process to sell its Botswana operations, setting up a potential contest among South Africa’s largest lenders as regional banks continue to expand while some global players retreat from parts of Africa.

item.title: Nigerian billionaire Rabiu’s ASR Africa builds 60-bed Customs hospital to support security sector reform
item.description: ASR Africa, the development initiative founded by Nigerian billionaire industrialist Abdul Samad Rabiu, has completed and commissioned a 60-bed hospital for the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) under its Security Sector Support Programme (SSSP). The new facility expands access to quality healthcare for security personnel, their families, and host communities in Northern Nigeria.

item.title: South Africa’s minimum wage hike sparks fresh fears over unemployment crisis
item.description: South Africa’s decision to raise its national minimum wage is intensifying debate over whether the policy protects workers or risks worsening one of the world’s most stubborn unemployment crises.

item.title: South Africa breaks into China’s $200bn fruit market with first major shipment
item.description: South Africa has shipped its first consignment of stone fruit to China, marking a significant breakthrough in agricultural trade between the two countries and the formal rollout of a new bilateral export protocol.

item.title: Europe targets Uganda energy boost with fresh $33 million investment
item.description: The European Union has pledged €30 million, about $32.7 million, to support the rehabilitation of the Nalubaale-Kiira hydropower complex in Uganda, signalling a renewed push to strengthen the country’s energy infrastructure and economic growth.

item.title: South Africa's largest lenders raise $322 million in new bank loss-buffer issuance
item.description: South Africa’s largest banks have raised about $322 million in new loss-absorbing debt as part of a central bank framework designed to ensure troubled lenders can be recapitalised without relying on taxpayer bailouts.
